title: In what order do these five expressions rise?
description: Five expressions are put in increasing order of their values. The value of each is found first, the values are ordered, and each value is matched back to its expression.
teaching_notes: One idea: to order expressions, find every value first and order the values. Do not judge by how big the numbers inside look.

video_script.why: The child orders expressions by comparing their values.
video_script.substitution: Find the value of each expression, order the values, then match each value back to its expression.
video_script.anchor: Five expressions to put in increasing order
video_script.payoff_line: The expressions rise in value from one hundred twenty divided by three to thirty five plus twenty five

final_answer.spoken: one hundred twenty divided by three, sixty seven minus twenty, sixty seven minus nineteen, five times eleven, thirty five plus twenty five

never_show: the five expressions in order before the answer beat
video_script.design: One idea: order expressions by their values. Assumes finding the value of an expression. Uses the method of the solved example on comparing. The five expressions stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; five expressions listed: (a) 67 − 19 (b) 67 − 20 (c) 35 + 25 (d) 5 × 11 (e) 120 ÷ 3

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.ask: the five expressions appear in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Five expressions are given. Arrange them in increasing order of their values.

beats.on_screen: the five expressions stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: five empty boxes in a row with a smallest end and a greatest end

marks.same: the five boxes appear with the words smallest and greatest at the ends

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='plan'/>First find the value of each expression. Then compare the values.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, five expressions, each made of two numbers and one operation.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expressions from the smallest value to the greatest

marks.find: the words smallest to greatest are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to arrange the expressions from the smallest value to the greatest.

marks.one: the first two values are written

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, find the value of each expression. Sixty seven minus nineteen is forty eight, and sixty seven minus twenty is forty seven.

marks.two: the first two of the other values are written

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, find the other three values. Thirty five plus twenty five is sixty, and five times eleven is fifty five. <bookmark mark='rest'/>One hundred twenty divided by three is forty.

marks.order: the five values are placed in order

narration: <bookmark mark='order'/>Step three, put the five values in order. They rise from forty to forty seven, forty eight, fifty five and sixty.

marks.match: each value is matched to its expression
marks.last: the last two values are matched

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step four, match each value back to its expression. Forty is one hundred twenty divided by three, and forty seven is sixty seven minus twenty.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Forty eight is sixty seven minus nineteen.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Fifty five is five times eleven, and sixty is thirty five plus twenty five.

beats.on_screen: check: five values, five expressions, each used once, each value greater than the one before

marks.check: a tick appears beside each of the five matches

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check the order. Each value is greater than the one before it, and every expression is used once.

marks.ans: the five expressions are written in order and the answer is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The expressions rise in value from one hundred twenty divided by three to thirty five plus twenty five.
